entities.summary:
Jan Latalski (1463–1540) was a medieval Bishop of Kraków, Poznań, Archbishop of Gniezno, and Primate of Poland.

A prominent figure in 16th-century Polish religious and political life, Latalski played a crucial role in shaping the Catholic Church's stance on the Protestant Reformation in Poland.

During his tenure, Latalski was a key advisor to King Casimir IV Jagiellon, who ruled over a vast territory that included present-day Poland, Lithuania, and parts of Ukraine.

Latalski's influence extended beyond Poland's borders, as he was involved in diplomatic efforts with the Holy Roman Empire and the Ottoman Empire.

The legacy of Jan Latalski can be seen in the establishment of the Polish Reformed Church, which emerged as a result of the Protestant Reformation and the subsequent wars between Catholics and Protestants in Poland.

'In order to maintain the unity of the Church, one must be willing to sacrifice one's own interests.' - Jan Latalski
